surprises.description: Q3 sales were $172.8 million, above both the preview’s $161.1 million consensus and the high end of the company’s $158–168 million guidance. The result was a clear upside to the preview’s conservative revenue setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 consolidated sales reached $172.8 million,” coming in “comfortably above the high end of guidance.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC was $13.6 million excluding tariff refunds, above the $10–13 million guidance range and the preview’s roughly $11.4 million estimate. That means the underlying operating result topped expectations even before counting the unexpected refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC excluding $5.4 million in DynaEnergetics tariff refunds was $13.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance: “adj. EBITDA attributable to DMC $10–13M”; preview estimate: “~$11.4M attrib.”

surprises.description: DMC received $5.4 million in DynaEnergetics tariff refunds despite the preview expecting no further refunds in Q3. The refunds added a substantial, non-recurring boost to the quarter’s reported EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA attributable to DMC was reported “excluding $5.4 million in DynaEnergetics tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “explicitly assumed no further refunds in Q3.”

surprises.description: Arcadia sales substantially exceeded the preview’s $67 million estimate: its reported 14% sequential increase implies roughly $77 million compared with Q2 sales of $67.4 million. Arcadia’s 14.7% margin also beat the preview’s 13.5% estimate, showing stronger growth and profitability than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arcadia building products sales rose 25% year-over-year and 14% sequentially,” and its adjusted EBITDA margin improved to “14.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview estimate: Arcadia sales “$67M” and “Q3 margin est. 13.5%.”

surprises.description: DynaEnergetics’ underlying margin reached 9.7%, above the preview’s 8.5% estimate and despite excluding tariff refunds. Cost savings and favorable mix produced a better operating margin than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: DynaEnergetics’ adjusted EBITDA margin “excluding refunds” improved to “9.7%” from 7.1% a year ago, aided by “cost savings and favorable mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview estimate: DynaEnergetics “Q3 margin est. 8.5%”; it also expected “no further refunds in Q3.”

surprises.description: DynaEnergetics volumes fell even as industry rig count and completion spreads increased 5–10%, indicating a loss of wallet share. That runs against the preview’s expectation that the tightening completions market would support DynaEnergetics volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DynaEnergetics volumes declined in the quarter despite industry rig count and completion spreads rising 5-10%, indicating a loss of wallet share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the tighter market “supports DynaEnergetics volume.”

surprises.description: NobelClad rebounded more strongly than the preview’s $25 million sales and 14.5% margin estimates suggested: sales rose 38% year over year, EBITDA surged 120%, and margin reached 15.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NobelClad sales jumped 38% year-over-year while adjusted EBITDA surged 120%, with margin expanding to 15.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview estimate: NobelClad sales “$25M” and “Q3 margin est. 14.5%.”

surprises.description: NobelClad disclosed a $72.4 million backlog, up from $63.5 million, and a quarterly record $16 million in U.S. Navy vessel construction orders. The preview described the backlog only as “healthy” and had no quantified backlog or record-order expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NobelClad's order backlog grew to $72.4 million from $63.5 million, including a quarterly record $16 million in U.S. Navy vessel construction orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said NobelClad backlog was “healthy” but “unquantified.”

surprises.description: Net debt fell sharply to $13.7 million from $30.5 million at Q2, supported by $16.6 million of free cash flow. This reversed the preview’s concern about H1 cash burn and the possibility of a third consecutive quarter of cash burn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt improved to $13.7 million, the lowest since the December 2021 Arcadia acquisition, down from $30.5 million at the end of Q2, supported by $16.6 million of free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted H1 operating cash flow of “–$10.3M” and warned that “a third straight quarter of cash burn materially worsens the put math.”

surprises.description: Management identified a $0.75 million defense/drone detonator contribution as a one-time “bluebird” and advised modeling DynaEnergetics margins 50–100 basis points lower because guidance includes no defense revenue. The preview did not anticipate this contribution or the resulting caution on future margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged a “$0.75 million defense/drone detonator contribution” as a non-recurring “bluebird” and advised modeling DynaEnergetics margins “50-100 basis points lower” since no defense revenue is in guidance.

surprises.description: Q4 guidance cites a California finishing-facility maintenance shutdown, a specific temporary headwind not identified in the preview. The preview did expect seasonal moderation, so the shutdown is an additional factor rather than a wholesale change to the Q4 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 guidance reflects “seasonal moderation and a California finishing facility maintenance shutdown.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q4 to be “seasonally weaker,” but did not mention a California facility shutdown.
